newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan institutions demand was 5x CANTV supply.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan institutions demand was 5x CANTV supply.

text.p: Demand by Venezuelan institutional investors for shares in Friday's $1 billion global offering by national telephone company CANTV outstripped supply five times, Venezuela's National Investment Fund (FIV) said.

While 85 percent of the orders placed by small private Venezuelan investors were met, "we could only give institutional investors between 10 and 20 percent," FIV privatisation manager Carlos Chacon said in an interview on Union Radio.
However, traders on the Caracas stock exchange said no conclusive number of shares had yet been released, stunting trade in the stock that many had expected would take the bolsa to new highs.
However, on Monday, the bolsa's index slipped 1.66 percent, while CANTV slipped four bolivars to close at 1716.00. In New York, CANTV's ADR slipped 1/2 to 25-3/8.

Some 73 million shares were sold in Venezuela, Chacon said, up from the originally slated 50 million. The total offering was originally planned for 289 million shares, spread between Venezuelan and international markets.
